days-between-dates.quickAnswer: Enter a start and end date-time and get the precise duration: for example, from 18 October 2026 09:00 to 25 October 2026 17:30 is 7 days and 8.5 hours - 176.5 hours, 10,590 minutes, or 5 business days. An optional toggle includes the end date in the day count.
keyFacts: Durations are computed from exact timestamps, so hours and minutes are precise - not rounded to whole days.
Business days count Monday to Friday only, using calendar math rather than a holiday list.
The 'include end date' toggle adds one day when you want both endpoints counted, as some contracts require.
If the end is before the start, the tool swaps them automatically and reports a positive duration.
Daylight-saving transitions can make a 'day' 23 or 25 hours long; this tool measures real elapsed time.
howTo: Enter the start date and time.
Enter the end date and time.
Tick 'include end date' if your use case counts both endpoints.
Read total days, hours, minutes, seconds and business days.
Use business days for project estimates and notice periods.
days-between-dates.formula:
Duration = end timestamp minus start timestamp.
Total days = duration / 86,400,000 ms.
Total hours = duration / 3,600,000 ms.
Business days = full weeks x 5 + weekdays in the leftover days (Mon-Fri).
Example: 2026-10-18 09:00 to 2026-10-25 17:30 = 7 days 8.5 hours = 176.5 hours.
days-between-dates.workedExample:
Start: 18 October 2026, 09:00. End: 25 October 2026, 17:30.
1. Timestamps subtracted: 7 days and 8 hours 30 minutes.
2. Total hours: 7 x 24 + 8.5 = 176.5 hours.
3. Total minutes: 176.5 x 60 = 10,590 minutes.
4. Total seconds: 10,590 x 60 = 635,400 seconds.
5. Business days: Monday 19 to Friday 23 October = 5 days (weekends excluded).
benefits: Timestamp precision settles 'exactly how long' questions for rentals, shifts and SLAs.
Business-day count is ready-made for work planning.
Handles overnight and multi-week spans without manual math.
Private and instant - no spreadsheet needed.
limitations: Business days exclude weekends only; public holidays are not in any list and are counted as business days.
Uses your device's time zone for both timestamps; convert first for cross-zone durations.
Daylight-saving transitions are measured as real elapsed time, which may surprise whole-day counts.
The 'include end date' convention varies by industry - confirm what your contract means.

faqs.q: Does it count the end date?
faqs.a: By default, no - from Monday 09:00 to Tuesday 09:00 is exactly 1 day. Tick 'include end date' to add one day when your convention counts both endpoints.
Full weeks contribute 5 business days each, and leftover days are checked one by one for Monday-to-Friday. Public holidays are not subtracted.

faqs.q: What if the end is before the start?
faqs.a: The tool swaps them automatically and reports the positive duration, so the order does not matter.

faqs.q: Can I use it for shift lengths?
faqs.a: Yes - enter clock-in and clock-out times, even overnight. The math handles spans past midnight.

faqs.q: Why do hours sometimes not equal days x 24?
faqs.a: Around daylight-saving transitions a calendar day can be 23 or 25 hours. The tool measures real elapsed time, which is the honest number.

faqs.q: Is this the same as the Date Calculator?
faqs.a: Related but different: this tool measures precise durations between two date-times including business days, while the Date Calculator shifts a date by N days.
